entry.dc:title: CANADA TUNGSTEN - CHANGE TO UNDERGROUND MINING & DESCRIPTION OF MINE-MILL PROCEDURES.
entry.dc:creator: Cummings W.
entry.dc:description: Canada's only current tungsten producer started up in 1962 with a small open-pit mine on the Flat River, 130 air miles north of Watson Lake, Yukon Territory. The orebody was in a contact-metamorphic skarn zone and contained about 1. 5 million tons of ore grading an estimated 2. 47% WO//3 and 0. 5% copper. Near the end of the open pit, a new zone was discovered on the lower limb of the same structure, and the decision to go underground was made in 1972. A continuing program of change and up-grading is necessary in the conversion from a seasonal open-pit mine with limited life to an underground operation with twenty years of reserves. Changes are necessary in plant and services as well as the mine. This paper sums up the changes in the operation since 1971 and outlines the changes yet to come.

entry.dc:title: Use of Explosives at the Kiruna Mine.
entry.dc:creator: Sundholm R.
entry.dc:description: The LKAB Company exploits two underground iron mines and one open-pit mine in the Swedish Lapland. Total output of these three mines is 60 million tons/yr of ore and gangue. Consumption of explosives at the three mines is significant and has spurred LKAB to produce its own explosives: output in 1975 consisted of 9,705 tons of ANFO explosive, 5,229 tons of explosive slurries and 9,936 tons of Kimit (a water-gel explosive called Tremite in the U. S. ). The use of Kermit was introduced by LKAB to solve the problem of fumes from blasting in the underground mines. The Kirma mine is briefly described, and the reasons that prompted LKAB to manufacture and use Kermit are explained.

entry.dc:title: Reclamation: A Challenge to Open-Pit Mining in Canada..
entry.dc:creator: Zahary G.
entry.dc:description: Open-pit mine reclamation criteria of legal, technical and esthetic nature are reviewed. The types of solid wastes resulting from mining operations are described. The results of research on the possibility of implanting a vegetal cover on highly acidic siliceous residues produced by uranium ore treatment plants at Ellito Lake, Ontario, are presented, demonstrating the success of a program of soil ph neutralization and the addition of nutritive elements.

entry.dc:title: GEOLOGY OF THE CARGILL PHOSPHATE DEPOSIT IN NORTHERN ONTARIO.
entry.dc:creator: Sandvik P.
entry.dc:description: The Cargill phosphate deposit, located 32 kilometers southwest of Kapuskasing, Ontario, was discovered by the Resource Development Group of International Minerals & Chemical Corporation in 1975 and has been evaluated through an extensive program of 190 drill holes, numerous chemical analyses, metallurgical tests, and engineering and economic studies. The deposit's general and structural geology as well as petrology are reviewed. A tentative open-pit mine, designed for preliminary feasibility studies, is estimated to contain a pobable phosphate-bearing deposit of 62. 5 million metric tons at an average grade of 19. 6 per cent P//2O//5.

entry.dc:title: UNIQUE APPLICATION OF SEISMIC METHODS IN AN OPEN-PIT MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Kim Y.S.
entry.dc:description: A feasibility seismic refraction and reflection field survey was conducted at the U. S. Borax Company open-pit mine, Boron, California by the writers during the weekend of March 13 and 14, 1976. This field survey was carried out as a preliminary investigation primarily for the purpose of evaluating and establishing the ability of such geophysical techniques to locate and outline the subsurface openings of the old room-and-pillar mining under the present open-pit. The value of such knowledge about the old underground workings is directly related to the safe and economical operation of the open-pit mine for the company.

entry.dc:title: DESIGNING OF OPEN-PIT MINES - THE OPEN-PIT MINE AT THE UDOKAN COPPER DEPOSIT.
entry.dc:creator: Sedlow M.G.
entry.dc:description: The Udokan copper deposit is one of the biggest deposits in the world with the copper grade of 1. 5%. The mining conditions are favorable for open-cast operations. Production of 35 million tons per year of ore or 90 million m**3 of ore and waste is due to be attained in two stages with the help of heavy-duty shovels and dumpers. With the deepening of the open-pit and greater distances, possible use of continuous-type transport facilities will have to be considered. All equipment, buildings and constructions must meet arctic conditions.

entry.dc:title: Industrial Tests of Different Types of the Top Structure of Permanent Rail Tracks.
entry.dc:creator: Volkov G.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: An experimental open-pit mine rail track sector with different construction of its top structure has been built at the Sarbay open-pit mine of the Sokolovsko-Sarbayskiy Ore Dressing Combine in Kazakhstan. It is designed for tracks with inclinations of up to 60 per 1000 and axial loads on the rolling stock of up to 35 t. Industrial tests of timber and - both serially produced and experimental strengthened - concrete sleepers laid on ballasts of different thickness have been staged. Results of experimental measurements of stresses in rails and sleepers, and of pressures on the basic area of the bed arising when the PE-2M traction unit moves over it are presented.

entry.dc:title: Computer Simulation of an Open-Pit Mining Process.
entry.dc:creator: Tarasiewicz S.
entry.dc:description: An approach to the way of forming a simulation model with the use of ″time slicing″ is presented. Before the simulation programmes are worked out the digital models of elementary units and technological structure configuration are formed. Then the model of technological process structure is represented in computer memory. As a result of this procedure a simulation programme for ODRA 1204 computer is worked out and tested. These programmes can be used to analyze mining technological processes of any open-pit mine.

entry.dc:title: ASBESTOS HILL-NORDENHAM STORY: THE OPEN-PIT MINE AT ASBESTOS HILL.
entry.dc:creator: Roussin R.
entry.dc:description: Annual production from the Asbestos Hill pit is 1,550,000 tons of asbestos ore, with a yield varying between 18 and 20%. The orebody was exposed at the top of a hill, and initial production started without having to remove any overburden. The final pit will be 2300 feet long by 1000 feet at the longest and widest points. The final depth will be 680 ft. A pit slope stability study was carried out and an average wall angle of 60-70 degrees must be maintained. Preshearing of final pit limits will produce good wall stability. Permanent access ramps will be 60 ft wide, with an 8% maximum grade. Geological conditions and the low rock temperature are the major causes of the operation's drilling and blasting problems.

entry.dc:title: PIT SLOPE DISPLACEMENT MONITORING: AN AID TO OPEN-PIT MINE OPERATION.
entry.dc:creator: MacRae A.
entry.dc:description: Slope failures exact a large, unpredictable sum from the open-pit mining industry every year, and fatalities and large-scale equipment damage are not the only forms of loss. Direct cost for removal of slide material is considerable, and indirects associated with rescheduling and lost production are significant over the long term. This article describes existing slope displacement monitoring systems and some new developments, including information on system accuracy, range, applicability, and cost, based on the author's past projects. Advantages and disadvantages of the systems are discussed, and suggestions are made for future improvements in this field.

entry.dc:title: DIRECT REDUCTION HEATS UP IN STEELMAKING.
entry.dc:creator: Miller J.
entry.dc:description: A mini-hydraulic slurry mining program that is scheduled to strip 265,000 cu yd of redeposited silt from the Caland open-pit iron mine near Aitkon, Ont. , is described. The program is a microcosm of an earlier project at the site - one of the largest preproduction dredging and water diversion projects in mining and construction history - but it will help Caland, an Inland Steel Co. subsidiary, obtain a new lease on mining life. For Marconflo, the Caland effort marks the first use of its slurry repulp and reclaim system at an open-pit mine - a new addition to a growing list of actual and conceptual slurry handling applications. A tandem set of Marconflo units, Dynajet 1000 capsule and a caisson 1000 jet, are briefly described.

entry.dc:title: DEFORMATION OF A CONTACT-METAMORPHIC ROCK MASS AT LOST RIVER, ALASKA.
entry.dc:creator: Jeremic M.
entry.dc:description: The generally accepted principles of rock mechanics are used to explain the failure mechanism of a contact-metamorphic rock mass complex undergoing ellipse stress deformation. The investigation was based on structural data collected in the field and obtained from old mining and exploration reports and studies. The approach used analyzes the rock-mass mechanics resulting from a Cretaceous geological event. It follows a stress ellipse model based on the tectonic forces, the geometry of the rock structure and natural stress induced by the structural dilation. The role of geological structure and induced stress in determining the mechanism and nature of deformation bears on open-pit mining operations. Their influence on the stability of the possible open-pit mine deserves careful attention. 9 refs.

entry.dc:title: GEOCHEMICAL AND GEOLOGIC RELATIONS OF GOLD AND OTHER ELEMENTS AT THE GOLD ACRES OPEN-PIT MINE, LANDER COUNTY, NEVADA.
entry.dc:creator: Wrucke C.
entry.prism:publicationName: U S Geol Surv Prof Pap
entry.dc:description: The distribution and association of gold and other elements at the Gold Acres open-pit mine was studied to determine the suites of elements introduced during mineralization and their bearing on the origin of this disseminated gold deposit. Unmineralized samples collected from outcrops in the Cortez Range and from a drill core in upper-plate rocks 5. 3 miles north of the open-pit mine provide a measure of background values for 31 elements; samples collected in an area of weak mineralization near Gold Acres were used to determine threshold concentrations. Geologic considerations and data on correlations indicate that the mine contains a gold suite consisting of gold, arsenic, boron, mercury and tungsten; a base-metal suite containing copper, lead, zinc, arsenic, bismuth, cadmium, iron, manganese, and molybdenum; and an iron-manganese suite of elements consisting of iron, manganese, arsenic, boron, chromium, cobalt, copper, nickel, scandium, titanium, yttrium, and zirconium. Refs.

entry.dc:title: Plotting Open-Pit Mine Plans by Means of a Device for Graphic Data Output from Computers.
entry.dc:creator: Bogachev A.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: A system of graphic man-computer interaction is proposed for utilization in solving problems of plotting open-pit mines by the method of selection. The article describes the experience of using such a system developed at the All-Union Institute of Mineral Prospecting Geophysics in application to geological and mining problems. The system of graphic interaction consists of a computer set, including a CRT display and a graphic data input device.

entry.dc:title: LASER SURVEY CONTROL OF DIVERSION TUNNEL DRIVE SAVES TIME AND MONEY AT KENNECOTT'S RAY MINE.
entry.dc:creator: Goff J.S.
entry.dc:description: Laser guidance systems for survey control of tunneling are quickly gaining wide acceptance in the mining industry. One method for control of curves, recently employed at the Ray open-pit mine of Kennecott Copper Corp. in Arizona, has apparently broken some new ground. The laser control system was put into action in driving a diversion tunnel for Mineral Creek, which flowed across the proposed northeast boundary of the Ray pit. Fluor Utah Inc. began the tunnel construction using conventional drill and blast methods in November 1970. Tunnel cross-section and length necessitated the use of rail-mounted equipment. Details of laser beam application in construction of the tunnel are described.

entry.dc:title: Simplified Method of Determination of the Slipping Surface and the Safety Margin Coefficient in an Isotropic Medium.
entry.dc:creator: Okatov R.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: A simplified analytical method is worked out for the determination of the safety margin coefficient when investigating the stability of spoil slopes and open-pit mine edges. A circular, cylindrical form of the slipping surface is accepted. This method is simpler than the generally accepted graphic solution.

entry.dc:title: ISUA, GREENLAND: CALCULATIONS OF GLACIER FLOW FOR AN OPEN-PIT MINE.
entry.dc:creator: Colbeck S.
entry.prism:publicationName: U S Army Cold Reg Res Eng Lab Res Rep
entry.dc:description: Investigation of the possibility of developing an open-pit mine along the edge of the Greenland Ice Cap. The response of the glacier to a sudden change in surface slope and thickness is calculated. The existing flow is diverted away from the mineral deposit but will increase when the excavation begins. It is calculated that 66 million cubic meters of ice must be removed to establish a stable profile beyond the pit.

entry.dc:title: The age of sulfide mineralization at Rossland, British Columbia
entry.dc:creator: Fyles J.
entry.dc:description: Mines near the city of Rossland in the West Kootenay district of southeastern British Columbia were important producers of copper and gold from 1894 to 1928 and of molybdenum since 1966 from an open-pit mine near the copper-gold camp. Eighteen new K-Ar dates of plutonic, dike, and volcanic rocks indicate that the age of the oldest pluton (the Rossland monzonite) is more than 90 m.y. and that all the other rocks are between 46 and 52 m.y. Geological relationships show that the molybdenite is older than the copper-gold mineralization. The molybdenite is about 48 m.y. because it is cut by 48.1 m.y. dikes and occurs in fractures which cut quartz diorite with an apparent age of 48.7 m.y. The copper-gold mineralization is younger than lamprophyre dikes with an average age of 48.2 m.y. and is thought to be about this age. Mineralization in the Rossland camp, therefore, is Tertiary and appears to be genetically associated with two bodies of quartz diorite and granodiorite formerly regarded as part of the Nelson plutonic suite. © 1973 Society of Economic Geologists, Inc.

entry.dc:title: Statistical Evaluation of the Interrelation Between Rock and Ore Volumes When Mining Deposits of Different Types.
entry.dc:creator: Arsent'ev A.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: A method is presented for quick evaluation of the possible boundaries of open-pit mines and the productivity of the mines as regards the volume of rock and mineral. The method consists in finding the coefficient of nonuniformity of overburden removal over a period and the ratio of useless rock extracted during the period of construction of an open-pit mine. Deposits with different bedding of ore bodies are classified and represented schematically and the influence of the thickness of the overburden on the coefficient of overburden removal is investigated by the method of modeling. For the initial period of operation the coefficient of nonuniformity of overburden removal is 1. 25 (until the extraction of about 40% of ore reserves).

entry.dc:title: Evaluation of the Stability of Open-Pit Mine Edges by the Dynamic Programming Method.
entry.dc:creator: Popov S.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: The way of constructing the weakest possible slope or edge surface of an open-pit mine is considered. It is based on the use of the method of dynamic programming. The slope is divided into N vertical prisms, and each of the boundaries of an elementary prism into m sections. The problem is formulated as follows: it is necessary to find in the region of the possible location of the weakest surface such a line, beginning at the base points and ending at the right-hand boundary of the prism N, along which the difference between the restraining and the shifting forces is minimal. The formulated optimality principle makes it possible to solve this problem. A program is compiles and tested in the BESM-4 computer codes for the realization of an algorithm. Variation of the rock properties during transition from one elementary prism to another is allowed.

entry.dc:title: Kinematic Features of Scooping Blown-up Rock by Single-Bucket Open-Pit Mine Excavators.
entry.dc:creator: Kubachek V.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: Results are presented of investigations of the operation of the excavators with nominal bucket capacity from 3 to 8 cubic meters, designed by the Uralmash Plant, carried out at various open pit mines in the USSR. It is found that when working blown-up rock by open-put mine excavators, scooping takes place mostly thanks to crumbling falling of the debris down the slope of a heap. This determines essentially the parameters of the trajectories of scooping, displacement and relations of the speeds of the drives of the lifting and thrust mechanisms. Lack of correspondence of the presently accepted relations between lifting and thrust speeds and the conditions of scooping of blown-up rock is made evident. Recommendations are given for limiting the speed of lifting to 0. 6-0. 65 m/s during scooping and for its increase during the performance of auxiliary operations. This will make an increase in the productivity and efficiency of the excavators possible.

entry.dc:title: Development of the Methods of Determination of Productivity of Open-Pit Mines.
entry.dc:creator: Arsent'ev A.
entry.prism:publicationName: Izvestiya Vysshikh Uchebnykh Zavedenii Gornyi Zhurnal
entry.dc:description: The case of maximum-intensity open-pit mining both in depth and in horizontal direction with a variable slope of the working edge is considered and the possible productivity of the mine is determined in the following way. First, the rational direction of the development of the extraction work in the open-pit mine is determined. Then the layout of the mining work for each level is constructed in accordance with two variants: that of maximum mineral extraction and of ensuring a minimum working area. The minimum time of level preparation is determined by means of graphs or analytical dependences. The volumes of ore extracted from the mine during the preparation of each level is calculated. The graphs of the growing volumes of the mineral in time are constructed and a curve of stabilized productivity is drawn. Its sector that has the greatest angle of inclination to the X-coordinate corresponds to the productivity of the mine that is the maximum possible for the given conditions.

entry.dc:title: A three-dimensional consideration of the stresses surrounding open-pit mine slopes
entry.dc:creator: Stacey T.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Rock Mechanics and Mining Sciences and
entry.dc:description: Models of open pits of circular and non-circular shape are analysed using the three-dimensional finite element method of stress analysis. The effects of different lateral latent stress fields and different plan radii of curvature of the slopes on the stress distributions are studied. Particular attention is paid to the circumferential stresses in the slope. It is found that the orientation of a non-circular pit with respect to the lateral stress field is very important when considering slope stability; the magnitude of tensile zones in the slope, and the presence of tensile zones in the pit floor both depend on this orientation. © 1973.

entry.dc:title: On the Type of Open-Pit Mine Loading Machines for Hard Rock.
entry.dc:creator: Spivakovskii A.
entry.dc:description: Designing of a face loading machine of continuous action for loading and conveying large-size rock pieces, resulting from blasting hard rock deposits in order to speed up and automate transportation, is considered. Two types of such machines are discussed: with scooping and raking working organs. It is recommended that one of the designs proposed, namely, a continuous-action machine with a blade rotor and paired raking paws, be adopted for development and manufacture. This machine would weigh about 200 t and its capacity would be 1500-1800 t/h.

entry.dc:title: MINE EVALUATION AND PRODUCTION SCHEDULING (MEPS).
entry.dc:creator: Bosman H.
entry.dc:description: Over the past five years, contributions from geologists and mining engineers were instrumental in the successful development of MEPS. It is a system of FORTRAN programs specifically designed to be used by mining personnel to solve geological and mining problems. MEPS is a flexible keyword-driven system. Extensive error editing procedures significantly reduce the time required to proceed from problem recognition to solution. Possibly the most attractive feature of MEPS is that computer solutions may be guided or selectively modified to obtain desired solutions. Some highlights of MEPS are: vocabulary that is familiar to mining people; geological data storage and retrieval; statistical analysis and variograms; contour maps of assays and geological horizons; trend surface analysis with residual evaluation; ore reserve calculations; open-pit mine design; marginal profitability calculations on pit walls; production scheduling; and vertical cross-section plots indicating pit outlines, ore grade contours and selected geological horizons.
